actions.label: fulltext
actions.text: In the NRPIC implementation of arXiv:2611.12831 particles and fields share a common global time step: in each step the spacetime solver advances the geometry from t^n to t^{n+1}, and the particle pusher then advances the ensemble over the same interval.
actions.evidence: VERIFIER2.md item 1: 781 kept the brief's inference 'so deep refinement slows everything down' and its [TO VERIFY] mark under a fulltext label. The source says only that the time step is common and global (L75, caption of Fig. 1) and how one step proceeds (L676); it does not say that deep refinement slows the run. The inference is not carried into the successor.

actions.label: fulltext
actions.text: arXiv:2611.12831 finds that its most compact cluster, y_c = 0.283 with fractional binding energy E_b/M_0 of about -0.0398, expands instead of forming the black hole reported for it in Ref. 1985ApJ...298...58S, and says that this discrepancy highlights the need for further investigation of the highly relativistic, nonlinear evolution of collisionless clusters.
actions.evidence: VERIFIER2.md section 2, stratum P: 574 was a noun phrase whose predicate 'the need for further investigation of' (L1140) was cut away. The successor is the whole sentence of L1140 with the result it qualifies.

actions.label: judgement
actions.text: From the construction of arXiv:2611.12831 at L967 (nabla^2 Phi_N = 4 pi rho_N, psi_bar = 1 - Phi_N, rho_bar_ADM = 2 rho_N psi_bar^-5) it follows in the continuum that nabla^2 psi_bar = -2 pi psi_bar^5 rho_bar_ADM [JUDGEMENT: one line of algebra, not a statement of the paper].
actions.evidence: VERIFIER2.md section 2, stratum M: 553 carried [JUDGEMENT] in its text under the label fulltext. The algebra is right (verifier and lead: nabla^2 psi_bar = -4 pi rho_N and rho_N = rho_bar_ADM psi_bar^5 / 2). Brief 12.8: a judgement is never upgraded to fulltext, so the successor has the label judgement.

actions.evidence: VERIFIER2.md section 2, stratum M: 145 ('peculiar speeds up to 0.4-0.5 c') made the mean and median of L2400-2402 a maximum. The successor gives them as mean and median.

actions.label: fulltext
actions.text: arXiv:2507.18312 asks whether a black hole can form after the time t_c of the central density divergence, once the evolution is continued past it after softening, and answers that its numerical simulations do not support this: the central layers pass through the origin and cross the infalling outer layers, which lowers the central density; for a typical peak it concludes that spherical shell crossing prevents black-hole formation at parametrically smaller delta_m unless the profile is sufficiently flat.
actions.evidence: VERIFIER2.md section 2, stratum Q: 169 ('2507.18312 says no for spherical shells') cut away the question it answers (L240) and was filed under paper 1609.01588. The successor states question and answer, under paper 2507.18312.

actions.evidence: VERIFIER2.md section 2, stratum M: 462 ('a variant with the auxiliary field B^i') had its subject cut away. The successor states it whole; the sentence begins at L381.

actions.label: fulltext
actions.text: arXiv:2609.14218 simulates primordial-black-hole formation in an early matter-dominated era in full numerical relativity from a curvature perturbation with ellipticity, a triaxial configuration, and finds with collisionless particles a threshold of black-hole formation smaller than the previous analytic estimate by an order of magnitude, while with a dust fluid the initial amplitude must exceed the analytic estimate by a factor of 2 for a horizon to appear before the computation crashes.
actions.evidence: VERIFIER2.md C1 reservation (b): 773 carried the label abstract and no locator. The abstract (L168-177) and the conclusions (L1200-1203) of 2609.14218 say what the successor says. Two parts of the brief's sentence are not said by this paper and are not carried: 'the analytic estimates disagree markedly among themselves' (L219 speaks only of analytic works 'with not necessarily valid perturbative approximations') and 'only this one full-NR particle calculation was found' (a statement about a literature search, not about the paper). Track A is told in an information note.

actions.label: fulltext
actions.text: arXiv:2611.12831 follows the collapse of two Jeans-unstable overdensities inside a common collisionless envelope through black-hole formation, accretion, binary inspiral and merger (a common horizon at about t = 64.175M) and the subsequent accretion onto the remnant, extracts the gravitational-wave strain at coordinate radius R = 40M, and calls the calculation an idealized example.
actions.evidence: VERIFIER2.md C1 reservation (b): 774 carried the label abstract and no locator. The abstract (L41-44), the results (L1360, L1362) and the conclusions (L1384-1391) say what the successor says. The brief's first clause, that AMR, GPUs and moving punctures 'let NRPIC continue long after black-hole formation and handle several black holes', is an inference from L30-33 and L700, not a statement of the paper, and is not carried. Core is told in an information note.

actions.label: fulltext
actions.text: arXiv:2611.12831 calls its two-overdensity calculation an idealized example and cautions that drag by the envelope could transfer angular momentum between the black-hole binary and the environment and drive faster coalescence; between t = 20M and 60M the summed orbital angular momentum of the holes falls by 27.3 per cent while the envelope, of zero net angular momentum at first, gains a comparable amount.
actions.evidence: VERIFIER2.md C1 reservation (b): 712 carried the label abstract, no locator, and a source outside the corpus (an alphaXiv overview). The successor keeps what the paper says (L1358, L1389). Not carried: 'no direct benchmark against established methods' (the paper compares Oppenheimer-Snyder collapse with the moving-puncture results of Staley et al., L919 and L1372, so this part is doubtful as worded), 'no item-by-item ablation' and 'no shear inside the clumps' (not found in the paper by the lead).
